title: Aurora Fintech outbound + objection handling scratchpad
content:
Note to self: quick, messy account sketch before I call Kira. Keep this informal — it's a working outreach blueprint and objection cheat-sheet for Aurora (midwest fintech, payments + risk tooling).

Account snapshot
- Company: Aurora Fintech (YC-ish style, ~220 employees)
- HQ: Columbus, OH (engineering split between OH + remote East Coast)
- Vertical: merchant payments + chargeback/risk detection for SMBs
- Why they might care: need lower-latency fraud scoring + on-prem/private options for regulated merchants; want to reduce cost of heuristics/rule engine and boost accuracy with model ensembles but procurement hates cloud vendor data exposure.
- Likely infra: AWS heavy (EKS + RDS), some customers ask for VPC-only integrations.
- Known pain from job post: "ML infra engineer (inference)" — suggests they run some models in prod, struggling with cost and scale.

Key contacts / roles to map
- Kira Thompson — Head of ML (primary outreach). Technical, cares about latency/SLOs and reproducibility.
- Dev: Marcus Li — infra lead (concerned about VPC, KMS, network egress).
- Prod Manager: Leah O'Connor — owns merchant integrations and contracts.
- Legal/Security reviewer: Svetlana Petrov — will gate private deploy.

Competitive signals
- Public blog: they use "open-source transformers + proprietary features" — likely rolling their own scoring pipeline.
- Job postings mention "quantized model deployment experience" and "gpu infra" — they may be experimenting with quantized models but not happy with ops.
- Possible vendor already in stack: small inference host (untested) + S3 based model store. Could be ripe for a more integrated solution.

Top hypotheses for outreach messaging
1) Cost + predictability: "We can cut per-token / per-embed cost by 30% with batching + caching tuned to your traffic patterns."
2) Private/in-house compliance: "Private deployment with customer-controlled KMS + audit logs; on-prem package for regulated merchants."
3) Latency/edge: "Consistent 95th %ile latency across bursts via dedicated pools and smart routing."
4) Faster rollouts: "Pin model versions and do canary rollouts without hand-rolling the infra."

Subject line ideas (A/B test)
- Short: "Reduce fraud scoring latency by 30% — quick idea"
- Risk-focused: "Private inference option for regulated merchants — Aurora + Redwood?"
- Curiosity: "How Aurora handles spikes in chargeback scoring"
- Social proof: "How fintechs cut inference cost; quick chat?"

First outreach email (very short, personalized)
- Draft A: "Kira — noticed your ML infra role + recent post about scaling model scoring. We help fintechs run model inference with predictable latency and private deployments (no customer data leaves your VPC). Mind 15 min to see whether this maps to what you're building? — Jordan"
- Draft B (technical): "Kira/Marcus — we can run your risk models behind your VPC, add KV/prefix caching to cut repeat-token compute, and support quantized variants for CPU/GPU tradeoffs. Can we run a 2-hour pilot on one scoring path?"

Follow-up cadences (4 touches)
1) Email (day 0) — short ask for 15 minutes.
2) LinkedIn connection + 2-sentence message (day 3).
3) Email with one-pager + suggested calendar slots (day 7).
4) Voicemail + final email (day 14) — include small hook (e.g., "I modeled your peak traffic and estimate a 25–40% cost win; short call to validate?").

Call cheat-sheet (for 15-min intro)
- 0–2 min: quick intros; confirm scope: are they scoring in real-time or batch?
- 2–5 min: pain check — congestion, cost, security concerns, SLO misses?
- 5–10 min: micro pitch — demo idea: run their scoring path in our sandbox; show 95p latency guarantee and cost delta.
- 10–14 min: next steps: propose PoC: 2-week smoke test using one model and one merchant flow, define success metrics (95th p latency <= X ms, cost per call <= Y).
- 14–15 min: ask about procurement/legal gate timeline and whether an NDA is necessary.

Objection handling (cheap, fast, conversational lines)
- "We already have an infra team / building this":
  - Response: "Totally makes sense — our customers often have infra teams we partner with. We can take the heavy lift off hands: deployment templates, SRE runbooks, canary rollouts so your team focuses on model quality, not infra plumbing."
- "Cost — vendor fees add up":
  - Response: "We model your traffic and show net unit economics — often the optimized runtime + KV/prefix caching and quantization pay for the contract in <3 months. I can run a free traffic-based estimate in 48 hours."
- "Data security / compliance concerns":
  - Response: "We offer a private deployment option where control plane is in your VPC and keys in your KMS/HSM. We also provide audit logs and integration playbooks for SOC2/PCI reviewers."
- "Integration complexity / time to ship":
  - Response: "We provide EKS/Helm charts, a small agent for on-prem, and a 2-week PoC path with a solutions engineer. Most first PoCs are under 10 days of engineering time from our side."
- "Latency / cold-starts / inconsistent p95":
  - Response: "Dedicated pools, warm-up hooks, and continuous batching tuned to your seq lengths keep tail latency predictable; we can instrument trace hooks into your stack for SLO verification."
- "We need model explainability / audit trails":
  - Response: "Inference logs with token-level traces (redacted), versioned model artifacts, and eval hooks tied to your prompt/inputs. We can produce an audit bundle for security reviews."

Pilot outline (2-week lightweight PoC)
- Week 0: Align success metrics + sign narrow NDA. Scope: 1 model, 1 merchant flow, synthetic dataset initial run.
- Week 1: Deploy private sandbox (VPC peering or ephemeral tunnel), run warm-up, collect baseline metrics.
- Week 2: Run live replay (traffic sample), measure p95, cost delta, produce short exec one-pager.
- Success criteria (example): p95 <= baseline * 0.9, per-call cost reduced by >= 20%, no data leaves VPC.

Internal TODOs (for me / SEs)
- Ask SE to precompute a cost model using their public traffic hints (approx daily calls per merchant). Put numbers in GH demo repo.
- Draft a 1-pager for Leah (procurement focus) highlighting procurement-friendly contract terms and data controls.
- Get legal template for NDA + template for SOC/PCI artifacts.
- Prep a short demo: show canary rollback + p95 dashboard + token-level cost breakdown.

Tactical notes (short-hand)
- If they say "we use AWS SageMaker endpoints": highlight ability to host models closer (private/dedicated) and predictable p95 vs autoscaling cold-starts.
- If they care about multi-region failover: discuss smart routing and cross-region fallback (cost vs latency tradeoffs).
- For procurement: default ask is "what's your procurement timeline?" — if >8 weeks, push for technical PoC first to build internal momentum.

Random outreach variants to paste into CRM (very short)
- "Kira — quick idea: I ran a back-of-envelope on Peak chargeback scoring and think we can cut cost by ~30% while keeping p95 latency. 15 min? — Jordan"
- "Marcus — curious how you handle model rollouts today. We do canary + automatic fallback for low-risk rollouts; this helped a payments customer avoid an outage. Chat?"

Notes-to-self:
- Do not promise specific %s until SE confirms on real traffic.
- Capture any security artifact requests immediately; send SOC2 + PCI checklist.
- If initial tone is "no budget": try to sell technical time-limited PoC for free and quantify value.

End of scratchpad. Save a copy to shared_drives/go-to-market/outreach-playbooks once cleaned up.
